summary: The message of an empty file area says what left it empty and offers the way out. src/finder/mod.rs: one pure function, `empty_message(&EmptyInput) -> EmptyMessage { title, detail, actions }`, replaces `empty_search_message` and the if/else chain in `render_content`. Rules in order: (a) a working Nushell filter that was given items and kept none: "No Items Pass the Filter" / "N items are hidden by the filter." with a Remove Filter button (plus the status tooltip's "More items match than the filter was given. Narrow the search." when the search was cut); (b) not searching: the Recents, Trash and folder strings, unchanged; (c) "Indexing…" (both wordings), "Searching…", "Nothing Found Before the Time Limit", unchanged; (d) new "The Search Was Cut Short" for a search cut at the result limit that lists nothing (the orchestrator's note); (e) "No Results" (`no_results`), whose line now says where the search looked ("The search looked only in “Projects”, and only for items of the kind Image.") with Search This Computer and/or Search Any Kind buttons; a contents search never names or offers a kind and adds that files over the size set in Settings aren't looked inside. `render_content`: the message branch also waits while a filter is still running over items (`!(self.filtering && self.unfiltered_len > 0)`), so placeholders show instead of a flash of "This folder is empty." or "No Results"; the buttons (ids empty-remove-filter, empty-widen-scope, empty-any-kind) are a wrapping centred row under the message and `run_empty_action` calls close_filter / set_scope(Computer) / set_kind(Any); a capture-phase mouse-down listener on the file area drops the second press of a double-click on one of them (`message_button_clicked`). `render_message`: the line under the title has the id `message-detail` with a label, the title is centred, and the message has 12 pt of padding at its sides. src/finder/bars.rs: the Kind button is outline + primary (accent) while a kind other than Any Kind narrows a name search; `MORE_THAN_FILTERED` is `pub(super)`. docs/manual.md: the message table (three new rows, No Results reworded), the Kind menu row, the filter paragraph, the Search Syntax paragraph, the tests bullet. tests/common/mod.rs: the settings folder a test program shares is emptied before its first window opens.
changelog: The file area's message said the wrong thing when a filter or a search setting left nothing to list. A folder or a search whose items a Nushell filter all hides now reads "No Items Pass the Filter", with how many items the filter hides and a **Remove Filter** button, where it read "This folder is empty." or "No Results". While the filter is still running, placeholders show instead of a flash of "This folder is empty." "No Results" now says what limited the search, as in "The search looked only in “Projects”, and only for items of the kind Image.", with **Search This Computer** and **Search Any Kind** buttons that search again without that limit. For a contents search it no longer suggests another kind, and says that files over the size set in Settings › Search engine aren't looked inside. A search that stopped at the result limit with nothing it could list reads "The Search Was Cut Short" instead of "No Results". The Kind menu's button is in the accent color while a kind other than Any Kind narrows the search. In a narrow pane the message keeps clear of the edges.
behaviour_changes: A folder, Recents, the Trash or a search whose items a working Nushell filter all hides reads "No Items Pass the Filter" with "N items are hidden by the filter." ("1 item is hidden…") and a Remove Filter button, where it read "No Items / This folder is empty." or "No Results". Remove Filter does what the filter bar's close button does (filter off, bar closed, keyboard to the files, the typed filter gone). When the search was cut at the limit the line adds "More items match than the filter was given. Narrow the search."

While a filter is still running over items of which it has kept none before (after going to another folder with a filter on, new search results, a Smart Folder with a filter opening), the file area shows placeholders (the columns in column view) instead of "This folder is empty." or "No Results". This lasts as long as the `nu` run, at most its 10 s timeout. An empty folder with a filter on still says "No Items" at once.

New, and the price of the line above: when "No Items Pass the Filter" is up and the list under it changes (typing on in a search, a folder that gains an item, a quiet rerun, another sort), the message gives way to placeholders for the length of the `nu` run (16 to 25 ms here for a small list) and comes back. On the trunk before, "No Results" or "No Items" simply stayed. See the note for filter-stale-keep-set.

"No Results" detail line: "Try a different name or search location." (was "…name, kind, or search location."); "The search looked only in “Folder”."; "The search looked only for items of the kind Image."; or both joined. Contents search: "Try different words or another search location." or the folder sentence, followed by "Files over the size set in Settings › Search engine aren’t looked inside."; never a word about kind. The folder named is `searched_folder()`, the one the search itself uses.

New buttons under "No Results": Search This Computer (only when the search is of one folder) and Search Any Kind (only for a name search with a kind other than Any Kind); at most two. They act like the scope bar's This Computer chip and the Kind menu's Any Kind (the kind is saved as a choice, also during a Smart Folder's search).

After a click on either, the keyboard stays where it was (typing goes on in the search field); the files get it if nothing in the browser had it, if it was outside the browser (split view's other pane), or if it was on the button (after a right click).
Tab skips the three buttons. They are for the mouse only: in the file area Return and Space are Open and Quick Look.

After one of the three buttons is clicked, left presses on the file area with a click count of 2 or more are ignored until a left press with count 1 arrives there. So the rest of a double-click on a button does nothing: it doesn't open the result that is now under the mouse, and doesn't press the other button, which moves to the middle where part of the first one was (in a wide pane too, not only a narrow one). A fast double-click on a result at the button's spot within the system's double-click time after the button was pressed is also ignored once.

New message "The Search Was Cut Short" / "The search stopped at the result limit before it came to an item it can list. Narrow the search, or raise Results shown in Settings › Search engine." (with a filter on: "…Narrow the search.") for a search with the `+` in its count and nothing listed, where it read "No Results". Rare in practice since scoped-search-special-folder-names.

The Kind menu's button is drawn in the accent colour (tinted background, accent border and text) while a kind other than Any Kind is chosen and the search is by name; unchanged (dimmed) for a contents search.

Every message in the file area, "Can't open this folder" and "Can't show the Trash" too: the line under the title has an accessibility label equal to its text and the test id `message-detail`; the message has 12 pt of padding at its sides, and a title that takes two lines in a narrow pane is centred (it was flush left, against the pane's edge).

Unchanged: "Indexing…" (both wordings), "Searching…", "Nothing Found Before the Time Limit", "No Recent Files", "The Trash Is Empty", "No Items", and "No Results" staying up while a search runs again. For the few milliseconds between a click on a button and the answer, "No Results" already describes the new scope or kind.

Manual: rows for No Items Pass the Filter, The Search Was Cut Short and The Trash Is Empty; No Results row reworded; a sentence each in the Kind menu row, the filter paragraph and the Search Syntax paragraph.
Tests only: a test program's settings folder (/tmp/fffinder-ui-config-<pid>) is emptied before its first window opens, so it no longer starts with what an earlier process with the same ID left there.
left_out: The title doesn't name the words searched for (the plan asked for "No Results for “q”" and "No files contain “q”"). Since search-skeleton-flash the message stays up while a search runs again, so a title with the words would name words that have no answer yet; three tests and the manual go by the exact title "No Results"; and "No files contain" would be false for a pattern with a filter in it. I agree with the implementer. If it is wanted, the answered words have to be kept with `search_stats`.
"Indexing…" without a count doesn't name the folder: adhoc-index-feedback owns that wording.
The contents "No Results" line names the file-size limit only, not the time limit: a search the limit ended has its own message.
No "Search Contents" / "Search Names" button, as the verifier decided.
Keyboard access to the three buttons: none (Tab skips them). Making Return and Space press them would need bindings that mask the files' Open and Quick Look.

No UI test of "The Search Was Cut Short": a search that is cut and lists nothing can't be made in the harness since scoped-search-special-folder-names. A unit test covers the rule; the wiring is `capped: stats.is_some_and(|s| s.truncated)`.
The Kind tint has no test (colours can't be read in the harness); pictures in light and dark.
CHANGELOG.md: not edited, as the guide says; the entry is in the commit message.

`cargo clippy --features term` not run: src/term is untouched and nothing it calls changed (the removed `empty_search_message` was private to mod.rs). Not compiled for macOS or Windows: no cfg-gated code is touched; the new field has one construction site (Finder::new); the new import (`Sizable`) is used on every platform.
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog: neither states anything this changes.

review_fixes: src/finder/mod.rs `render_message`: in a narrow split pane the new, longer titles ("No Items Pass the Filter") took two lines flush left against the pane's edge, under a centred line of text that also touched the edges. The title is centred and the message has 12 pt of padding at its sides (pictures: …-review-narrow-filter.png, …-review-narrow-buttons.png). New test a_message_and_its_buttons_fit_a_narrow_pane, which also pins that the two buttons wrap.

tests/controls.rs: new test a_double_click_on_a_button_under_no_results_doesnt_press_the_next_one. The implementer had left this half of the double-click guard without a test because it seemed to need a stacked layout. It doesn't: when Search This Computer finds nothing either, the one button left is centred where the right part of the first one was, in a pane of any width. Without the guard the second click pressed Search Any Kind.

src/finder/mod.rs `render_content`: the folder named in "No Results" comes from `searched_folder()`, which live-search-results put on the trunk for the search itself, instead of a second copy of the same test.

tests/common/mod.rs `isolate_settings`: a_filter_that_keeps_nothing_says_so_and_offers_to_remove_it failed once in about twenty runs with "5 items are hidden by the filter." The cause was not the test or the change: each test program points settings at /tmp/fffinder-ui-config-<pid>, which was created and never emptied, and tests/settings_file.rs turns writing on and toggles hidden files. PIDs repeat (pid_max is 32768 here), so a program started with the settings.json an earlier one with its PID had left. Reproduced on purpose by making the folder for the test program's own PID before `exec` (5 items), and gone with the fix (4 items). The folder is now removed before it is created.

docs/manual.md, No Items Pass the Filter row: "A filter that is still running hasn't hidden anything yet" wasn't true (what it kept last still hides rows); it now says that placeholders show while the filter is still running over the items.
Commit message: the paragraphs on the narrow pane, on the other button (not only in a narrow pane) and on the tests' settings folder; the Changelog paragraph has the narrow pane.
Rebased twice with no conflicts: onto 153eb8f (live-search-results) before the review, and onto d85ca95 (choose-nu-path ca4fbee, result-tie-break d85ca95) before the check.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the tree of the trunk commit f60d2e4: 687 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The implementer's commit was 07825ca on 60df179. The new tests fail without the change: with the diff of src reversed, six of the eight UI tests failed for the reasons listed under tests, an_empty_folder… stopped at the missing id, and the collapsed-group test passed (it guards the change against itself); I then took out one piece at a time (the guard's stop_propagation, the padding, `&& self.groups.is_empty()`, `&& self.unfiltered_len > 0`) and each made the test named for it fail. The new UI tests ran under seeds 0, 3, 11, 77 and 4242 and in sixty more runs with three programs at once; the one failure among them was the stale settings folder (see review_fixes), and none since it is emptied. Pushed to origin (d85ca95..f60d2e4).

The three ways I thought this could hurt a user, and what I found. (1) A real double-click swallowed by the new guard: no. Only left presses with a count of 2 or more are dropped, only while the flag is set, and any left press with count 1 on the file area clears it; a count-2 press there always follows a count-1 press at the same spot, which reaches the listener unless it landed on something that occludes the files (a menu's own items, a dialog), and then the count-2 press is a stray one anyway. A context menu's layer doesn't occlude outside the menu, so the press that dismisses it reaches the file area too. I tried clearing the flag on presses of the other buttons as well and took it out again: it bought nothing. (2) Placeholders or no message for ever because of the new filter guard: no. `filtering` is set only by `start_filter` and cleared by the run's end, `set_filter` and `nu_changed`, the run has a 10 s timeout, and a run over no items never holds the message back. (3) The keyboard or the user's place lost after a click on a button that then vanishes: the focus rule is the scope bar's plus the right-click case, tested; Search Any Kind saves the kind like the menu does; Remove Filter throws the typed filter away like the filter bar's close button does.

Deviations from the plan of record that I let stand: the title stays "No Results" (see left_out); the guard is `!(self.filtering && self.unfiltered_len > 0)`, narrower than `!is_filtering()`, so that an empty folder or a search that found nothing doesn't flash placeholders for the one step a run over no items takes; `filtered` also wants `self.groups.is_empty()`; the title id is the existing `message-title`; the button reads "Search Any Kind"; the buttons are no tab stops; the double-click guard is not in the plan.

For briefs still to come:
- collapsed-groups-empty-view: the message branch of render_content is now `self.rows.is_empty() && !self.loading && !self.awaits_first_results() && !(self.filtering && self.unfiltered_len > 0)`; swap only the first term for shows_nothing(). `filtered` in the EmptyInput has `&& self.groups.is_empty()`, which becomes spare once headers show. The message is `self.render_message(..).when(!buttons.is_empty(), ..)`: the context menu goes on that Div, whose 12 pt of side padding is inside it, so its hitbox still covers the file area. Check what a right-click on one of the three buttons does once the menu is there (today it gives the button the keyboard). Until your change, a search with every group collapsed reads "No Results" with the new line and buttons about scope and kind, which is as wrong as the old line was. an_item_in_a_collapsed_group_isnt_hidden_by_the_filter only asserts that empty-remove-filter is absent, so it holds when headers show instead.
- adhoc-index-feedback: the arm to reword is `None if input.partial => plain("Indexing…", "Results appear when indexing finishes.")` in `empty_message` (src/finder/mod.rs). The searched folder's name is already an input (`scope_folder`); add your flag as another EmptyInput field: the unit tests build inputs with `name_search(&location)` and struct update, so a new field touches only that helper. a_search_cut_short_with_nothing_listed_doesnt_say_no_results pins the order of the rules and that only "No Results" and the filter's message have buttons. If you keep `searching` true while a retry is pending, look at `awaits_first_results()` and `looking`.
- filter-stale-keep-set: the empty-state message can no longer show while a run is out over items; render_content's message branch has `&& !(self.filtering && self.unfiltered_len > 0)`. So in your cases (a), (b) and (c) the area shows placeholders (the columns in column view) from the rows changing to the run's answer whenever the stale keep-set leaves no row; rows it happens to keep still show. a_filter_that_is_still_running_doesnt_say_nothing_passes (tests/controls.rs) holds a run back without a stand-in script: it calls `navigate` inside `ui.window` and steps `ui.cx.executor().tick()` until `is_filtering()`, which is right after the listing's continuation and before the filter's task is first polled. It pins both halves; don't widen the guard to plain `!is_filtering()`, or an empty folder flashes placeholders. Left for you: when the rows are the same place's and the last run kept none of them, every new run (typing on in a search, a folder gaining an item, a quiet rerun, a re-sort, since `filter_source` holds the paths in order) shows message, placeholders, message. If you tie the keep-set to its place, that is the case to keep calm, for instance by leaving the message up with its old count until the run answers. `nu_changed` (choose-nu-path) resets the filter fields too.
- stray-double-click-opens-file: `Finder::message_button_clicked` and the `capture_any_mouse_down` listener on the file area (`#content` in render_content) guard the three message buttons only: `run_empty_action` sets the flag, the next left press with count 1 on the file area clears it, and until then left presses with a count of 2 or more are stopped in the capture phase. A general guard can replace both; a_double_click_on_a_button_under_no_results_opens_nothing and …_doesnt_press_the_next_one should keep passing (they use `ui.second_click`). What I read in the kit: a context menu's layer is a window-sized div without `occlude()` (gpui-component menu/context_menu.rs, DeferredMenu), so a press outside an open menu dismisses it and also reaches the row under it; the menu itself and dialogs occlude. `window.double_click(id)` sends down and up with count 1, then with count 2, at one point.
- focus-lost-recovery: a right-click or middle-click on a button under the message gives that button the keyboard and a ring (the kit's Button prevents the default only for left presses). `run_empty_action` hands the keyboard to the files when the button is then clicked, but when rows arrive by themselves (a quiet rerun, a folder refresh, a filter's run ending) the button goes with the keyboard on it. To get there in a test: `ui.right_click("empty-widen-scope")`, then `ui.snapshot("empty-widen-scope").focused() == Some(true)`. Picture: …-review-right-click-ring.png.
- search-start-no-flash, stale-rows-on-place-change: the message reads `self.searching`, `search_stats`, `unfiltered_len`, `filtering` and `groups` when it is drawn, behind the condition quoted above; its buttons call set_scope and set_kind (which go through run_new_search) and close_filter. Rows kept on screen for a grace period keep the message away by themselves (`rows.is_empty()`).
- regex-content-search, or anything that adds a search mode: `no_results` decides the line and the buttons from `contents`, `scope_folder` and `kind`.
- search-settings-without-effect, search-settings-hints-steppers: two lines name settings by their labels and are pinned by unit tests: "Files over the size set in Settings › Search engine aren’t looked inside." (the contents "No Results"; the search-truncation-honesty record says files over 10 MB are never searched whatever the setting says, so the line is exact only once that is fixed) and "…raise Results shown in Settings › Search engine." ("The Search Was Cut Short", like the status bar's tooltip).
- every brief with UI tests: tests/common/mod.rs `isolate_settings()` now empties /tmp/fffinder-ui-config-<pid> before a test program's first window opens. A lane that isn't rebased onto f60d2e4 yet can still start a test program with a stale settings.json: about 3,560 such folders are in /tmp, 197 with a settings.json, 37 of those with show_hidden true. The sign is a test that counts the fixture's four items and sees five (".secret"), once in a long while, and passes when run again. The old folders (20 MB) do no harm to rebased lanes; they can be deleted when no test program is running.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change unless it says otherwise):
- The "Open System Settings" button under "Can't show the Trash" can be reached with Tab, but Return and Space don't press it: in the file area they are Open and Quick Look. The three new buttons avoid this by not being tab stops; a right-click still puts the keyboard and the ring on them, and Return and Space don't press them either (new with this change, by the same cause).
- With every group collapsed the file area says "No Items" or "No Results" (collapsed-groups-empty-view).
- With "No Items Pass the Filter" up, a list that changes under the filter shows placeholders for the length of the run (new with this change; see behaviour_changes and filter-stale-keep-set).
- A results view sent from Nushell that has no items left says "No Items. This folder is empty.", though it isn't a folder.
- In the Trash, with a filter that hides every item, the Trash bar's Empty… button and the menu's item are off (they go by `rows.is_empty()`), although the Trash has items.
- The scope bar's folder chip is never cut short: a folder with a long name takes a line of its own and runs past the pane's edge (…-review-long-folder-name.png, at 900 pt).
- In a pane about 150 pt wide the messages' titles take two or three lines (now centred and clear of the edges).
